segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now faith is the reality of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For by it the ancients had witness borne to them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith we understand that the universe was set in order by God’s word, so that what is seen did not come into being from things that are visible.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, and through it witness was borne that he was righteous, God himself bearing witness over his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Enoch was taken away so that he did not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him away. For before he was taken away, witness is borne that he had pleased God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever approaches God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Noah, warned by God about things not yet seen, in reverent fear built an ark to save his household. Through this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that accords with faith.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and set out for a place he was going to receive as an inheritance, and he set out not knowing where he was going.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith he lived as a resident foreigner in the land of the promise, as in a land not his own, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith, together with Sarah herself, he received power to father offspring, even past the normal age, since he considered faithful the one who had promised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore from one man, and one as good as dead at that, there were born descendants like the stars of the sky in number and like the countless sand along the seashore.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All these died in faith, without receiving the promises, but they saw them from afar and greeted them, and they confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For people who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If they had been thinking of the one they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But as it is, they long for a better one, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was offering up his one and only son,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he to whom it had been said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Through Isaac your offspring will be named.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He reasoned that God was able to raise people even from the dead, and from the dead, figuratively speaking, he did receive him back.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, spoke of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king’s edict.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: choosing to be mistreated along with the people of God rather than to have the short-lived enjoyment of sin,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: considering the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he held firm as one who sees him who is unseen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if over dry land, but when the Egyptians tried it, they were swallowed up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been circled for seven days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who had disobeyed, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And what more shall I say? For time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, routed foreign armies.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Women received their dead back by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing to accept release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Still others experienced mocking and flogging, and even chains and prison.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and in holes in the ground.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all these, though witness was borne to them through their faith, did not receive what was promised,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: since God had provided something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect apart from us.

notes.phrase: the reality of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen
notes.traditional: the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (KJV); the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen (most modern versions)
notes.note: Most modern versions make faith an inner state: “assurance” and “conviction.” In the usage of the period the first noun normally names something objective, what underlies a thing or gives it substance, and the second means proof or demonstration, not the feeling of being convinced. Many commentators favor this objective sense, but scholarship is divided and “assurance” is still widely defended.

notes.traditional: obtained a good report (KJV); were commended; received approval
notes.note: The verb is the ordinary one for giving testimony, used here and in verses 4, 5 and 39 for the favorable witness that God or Scripture bears to these figures. Modern versions usually paraphrase as “were commended” or “received approval,” which states the sense fairly. The witness language is kept because the author builds on it, arriving at the “cloud of witnesses” in 12:1.

The Greek is literally “the ages,” a time-word that here and in 1:2 stands for the whole created order, as standard lexicons recognize. Older versions have “the worlds”; several modern versions also have “the universe.”

notes.phrase: together with Sarah herself, he received power to father offspring
notes.traditional: By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive
notes.note: The traditional rendering makes Sarah the subject. But the Greek phrase rendered “to father offspring” is the regular idiom for the male role in conception, and Abraham is the subject of the verses on either side. The edition translated here prints “Sarah herself” in a form meaning “together with Sarah”; in the earliest manuscripts that form and the subject form were written identically, and some manuscripts add “barren.” Both readings have strong scholarly support.

The word means the only one of its kind; its second half comes from the word for “kind,” not “beget,” though a minority of scholars have recently defended “only begotten.” Abraham also had Ishmael, so Isaac is “one and only” as the unique son through whom the promise was to run.

The Greek is literally “in a parable.” It may mean simply “in a manner of speaking,” since Isaac did not actually die. It may also mean “as a symbol,” so that Isaac’s return prefigures resurrection, perhaps that of Christ. The rendering leaves both open.

notes.phrase: bowed in worship over the top of his staff
notes.traditional: worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff
notes.note: The author quotes Genesis 47:31 in its Greek form. The Hebrew consonants there can be read as either “staff” or “bed”; the Greek translators read “staff,” while the traditional Hebrew vocalization gives “bed.” The verb names a physical bowing in reverence, here directed to God.

The phrase may mean abuse suffered for the sake of the coming Christ, or abuse of the same kind that Christ himself bore (compare 13:13). It may also echo Psalm 89:50–51, where God’s “anointed” is reproached, so that Moses shares the disgrace of God’s anointed people. The author does not explain how Moses knew of Christ, and interpreters differ.

Greek has one word-family where English has two (righteous and just, righteousness and justice). Since the list concerns judges, kings and prophets, the phrase most likely means that they ruled or judged justly, as many modern versions take it. It could also mean more generally that they did what was right.

notes.phrase: Others were tortured, refusing to accept release
notes.note: The women who received their dead back are the widow of Zarephath and the woman of Shunem (1 Kings 17; 2 Kings 4). The verb for “tortured” refers to being stretched on a frame and beaten. Most interpreters see an allusion to the martyrs of the Maccabean period, who according to 2 Maccabees 6–7 refused to save their lives by renouncing the Law and died in hope of resurrection.

notes.traditional: they were sawn asunder, were tempted
notes.note: Many manuscripts add “they were tested” (KJV “were tempted”) before or after this phrase. The edition translated here omits it, judging it a copying error. Jewish tradition held that the prophet Isaiah was sawn in two.

candidates.reason: The passive is rendered “commended,” “approved,” “attested” or “well spoken of” across Hebrews, Acts and 3 John, and the link to the “witnesses” of 12:1 depends on a fixed choice.
Translations vary among “seed,” “offspring” and “descendants,” and the arguments in Galatians 3 and Romans 4 and 9 depend on the same word being recognizable in the Genesis citations.

With πάροικος and ξένος it forms a cluster (here, 1 Peter 1:1 and 2:11, Ephesians 2:19) rendered as “exiles,” “sojourners,” “strangers,” “aliens” or “pilgrims,” and the cluster needs fixed, distinct English.
It recurs at Hebrews 10:33 and 13:13 and Romans 15:3 with versions split among “reproach,” “disgrace,” “abuse” and “insult,” and the Hebrews occurrences are deliberately linked.
